bib.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed. Table 9/10/11 numeric grids and Figure 20/21/22 plot text read only by header and sample rows; individual cells not transcribed beyond those cited.

question: Can learning image representations from raw natural-language supervision at web scale give a model that transfers zero-shot to many vision tasks, as GPT-style pretraining does in NLP?
hypothesis: Scalable pretraining directly on web text paired with images can produce a breakthrough in computer vision similar to that in NLP, with task-agnostic zero-shot transfer.
contributions: CLIP: a simplified ConVIRT-style contrastive pretraining, 5 ResNets and 3 ViTs trained from scratch
Zero-shot transfer via natural-language class prompts, benchmarked on 30+ datasets
Study of scaling, linear-probe representation quality, robustness to distribution shift, human comparison, data overlap, bias and surveillance probes
Release of code and pre-trained weights

method.summary: CLIP trains an image encoder and a text encoder from scratch with a symmetric InfoNCE contrastive loss on 400M web (image, text) pairs (WIT). At test time class names are embedded with prompt templates to form a zero-shot linear classifier. Evaluated on 30+ datasets via zero-shot, linear probes, robustness shifts, human comparison and overlap analysis.
method.task: contrastive image-text pretraining; zero-shot image classification and transfer

datasets.name: WIT (WebImageText)
datasets.source: publicly available internet sources; built from 500,000 queries, up to 20,000 pairs per query; not released
datasets.preprocessing: random square crop from resized images only augmentation; text lower-cased BPE; base queries are words occurring >=100 times in English Wikipedia plus bigrams with high PMI, Wikipedia article titles above search volume, and WordNet synsets

datasets.preprocessing: kept only images with natural-language English titles and/or descriptions; used for ablation (Table 12) and Visual N-Grams comparison

datasets.size: see Table 9 for per-dataset train/test sizes
datasets.split: validation split for lambda sweep then merged into train

Flickr30k, MSCOCO (5k test)

models.name: CLIP RN50, RN101, RN50x4, RN50x16, RN50x64
models.architecture: modified ResNet-D image encoder (antialiased rect-2 blur pooling, attention pooling instead of global average pooling) + 12-layer text Transformer; EfficientNet-style equal scaling of width, depth and resolution for x4/x16/x64
models.init_from: scratch (no ImageNet weights, no pretrained text encoder)

models.name: CLIP ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16, ViT-L/14, ViT-L/14@336px
models.architecture: ViT (Dosovitskiy) with extra layer norm on patch+position embeddings and different init; same text Transformer
models.init_from: scratch; L/14@336px: continues from ViT-L/14 for 1 extra epoch at 336px

models.name: Text encoder (base)
models.architecture: 12-layer 512-wide 8-head Transformer with masked self-attention; EOS token activation layer-normed then linearly projected

other.note: only width scaled with image encoder, depth not scaled

models.name: LM RN50 (autoregressive baseline)
models.architecture: ResNet-50 output projected into four prefix tokens to an autoregressive LM

other.note: same data and epochs as CLIP

models.name: Evaluated comparators: EfficientNet/Noisy Student, Instagram ResNeXt, BiT-S/M, ViT-21k, SimCLRv2, BYOL, MoCo, VirTex, ResNet

other.count: 66 models in the linear-probe study; 56 non-CLIP

training.objective: symmetric cross-entropy over N x N cosine-similarity logits (InfoNCE/N-pair), temperature learned as log-parameterised scalar
training.optimizer: Adam with decoupled weight decay (applied to all weights not gains or biases); beta1 0.9, beta2 0.999 (ResNet) / 0.98 (ViT), eps 1e-8 (ResNet) / 1e-6 (ViT)
training.precision: mixed precision; half-precision Adam statistics; half-precision stochastically rounded text encoder weights; gradient checkpointing
training.regularisation: temperature initialised to 0.07 and clipped so logits scale <= 100; no nonlinear projection head; random square crop only
training.compute: RN50x64 18 days on 592 V100; largest ViT 12 days on 256 V100; models span ~44x ResNet compute; 12.8 billion images seen over 32 epochs

other.hparam_search: grid, random and manual tuning on ResNet-50 for 1 epoch, then adapted heuristically for larger models
other.dup_detector: separate ResNet-50 with weight norm, GELU, anti-aliasing; batch 1,712, ~30M images, InfoNCE temperature fixed 0.07

inference.decoding: zero-shot: softmax over cosine similarity (scaled by tau) between image embedding and class-text embeddings; classifier cached once per dataset
inference.temperature: learned tau, clipped at 100 as scale
inference.samples: single deterministic evaluation per model; seeds not stated
inference.prompting: default template 'A photo of a {label}.'; dataset-specific templates; ensembles averaged in embedding space (80 prompts for ImageNet)

parameters.linear_probe: scikit-learn L-BFGS logistic regression, max 1000 iterations, L2 lambda swept 1e-6 to 1e6 in 96 log steps via parametric binary search to 8 steps/decade on validation split
parameters.few_shot_levels: 1,2,4,8,16 (up to 128 and full in robustness study)

other.note: OCR datasets: quotes around the text to recognise; retrieval: 'a photo of' prepended to captions (+1-2 R@1)

metrics.name: zero-shot top-1 accuracy
metrics.definition: class chosen by highest image-text cosine similarity over dataset class names

metrics.name: linear-probe accuracy
metrics.definition: logistic regression on penultimate-layer (pre-projection for CLIP) features

metrics.name: effective robustness
metrics.definition: accuracy under distribution shift above what logit-linear fit on ImageNet accuracy predicts (Taori et al. 2020)

metrics.name: contamination effect
metrics.definition: accuracy on All minus accuracy on Clean, with one-tailed binomial test and 99.5% Clopper-Pearson CIs

metrics.name: Recall@K
metrics.definition: image/text retrieval Recall@K (K = 1, 5, 10) on Flickr30k and MSCOCO 5k

metrics.name: per-dataset metric
metrics.definition: accuracy, mean per-class accuracy, mAP or ROC AUC per Table 9 (Hateful Memes: ROC AUC on dev set)

baselines: BiT-M/S, ViT-21k, SimCLRv2, BYOL, MoCo, Instagram ResNeXt, VirTex
eval.protocol: Single runs; no seeds or variance reported for training. Overlap test with Bonferroni correction. Authors concede they queried full validation sets during development.

limits: Zero-shot CLIP on average only competitive with a linear probe on ResNet-50 features, well below SOTA; ~1000x more compute estimated to reach SOTA (Sec 6).
Weak on fine-grained (cars, flowers, aircraft), counting, satellite, tumor, traffic-sign and distance-to-car tasks; near chance on some novel tasks.
Brittle on truly out-of-distribution data such as MNIST (88%).
Can only choose among supplied class names; cannot generate novel outputs.
Poor data efficiency; 12.8B images seen over 32 epochs.
Few-shot via linear probes drops below zero-shot, unlike humans (54% to 76% from 1 example).
Full validation sets were queried during development, so zero-shot claims are not clean; the 27-dataset suite is co-adapted to CLIP.
Training data are unfiltered, uncurated internet pairs and encode social biases; WIT is not released.
Overlap detector recall could not be checked across 400M examples.
No training seeds or variance reported; hyperparameters tuned on ResNet-50 for 1 epoch and adapted heuristically.
Dated: results compare to 2020-era models; no comparisons to later image-text models.

T_f = text_encoder(T)  #[n, d_t]
I_e = l2_normalize(np.dot(I_f, W_i), axis=1)
T_e = l2_normalize(np.dot(T_f, W_t), axis=1)
logits = np.dot(I_e, T_e.T) * np.exp(t)
labels = np.arange(n)
loss_i = cross_entropy_loss(logits, labels, axis=0)
loss_t = cross_entropy_loss(logits, labels, axis=1)
loss   = (loss_i + loss_t)/2
